pins.head: SET THE BENCH FIRST
pins.title: Epoxy Resin Tips: Set the Bench Up Before You Open a Bottle
pins.desc: Epoxy resin tips about mess all come back to the bench. Cover the whole surface so a drip lands on something you can peel, keep the cups, stir stick and scale within reach of one hand, and put the gloves and paper towel where you can grab them without touching a handle. A lidded tote underneath keeps the kit together between pours. Contains affiliate links. #EpoxyResin #ResinArt #CraftRoom
pins.alt: A corner bench covered with a pale silicone mat holding two clear plastic mixing cups, a wooden stir stick, a digital kitchen scale with a blank display, an open box of disposable gloves and a roll of paper towel, with a clear lidded storage tote on the shelf underneath.

pins.head: PEEL, DO NOT PUSH
pins.title: Resin Art for Beginners: Wait Longer Before You Pull the Mold
pins.desc: Resin art for beginners goes wrong at the demold more often than at the pour. A casting that feels hard can still flex, and forcing it out leaves a dented edge and a stretched mold. Give it the full cure, then peel the silicone back from one corner rather than pushing on the face. Wash the mold in warm soapy water and let it dry upside down. Contains affiliate links. #ResinArt #ResinMolds #DIYCrafts
pins.alt: A dark slate worktop with a clear hexagon resin casting sitting beside a pale flexible silicone mold peeled back off it, a folded grey cloth to one side and a stoneware bowl of soapy water holding a small wooden-handled brush.

pins.head: START UNDER THE BED
pins.title: Dorm Room Storage Ideas: Start With the Space Under the Bed
pins.desc: Dorm room storage ideas usually start on the walls, but the biggest empty volume in the room is under the bed. Soft bins on casters roll out without lifting, so off-season clothes and spare bedding stop living on the only chair. A narrow cart on wheels holds towels and everyday things and tucks back in when you need the floor. Contains affiliate links. #DormRoom #StorageIdeas #SmallSpaceLiving
pins.alt: The corner of a small bedroom with two grey fabric storage boxes on casters tucked under a wooden bed frame, a white three-tier rolling cart beside it holding folded towels and a small potted succulent, a hanging pocket organiser on a pale door and a jute runner on wood flooring.

pins.head: PRIME THIN, PAINT SHARP
pins.title: Miniature Painting Tips: Thin Primer Keeps the Detail Visible
pins.desc: Miniature painting tips are mostly about what happens before the colour. A thin even coat of primer leaves the sculpted edges crisp, while one heavy pass fills the lines you were going to pick out. Mount the models on corks so you can turn them without touching the surface, and wash each brush to the ferrule while the paint is still wet. Contains affiliate links. #MiniaturePainting #PaintingMiniatures #BrushCare
pins.alt: Three small grey primed knight miniatures standing on cork bases on a light oak desk, with a pale ceramic dish behind them holding four fine detail brushes with plain wooden handles, a white mixing palette and an open glass jar of pale brush soap.

pins.head: FURNITURE MAKES THE WALLS
pins.title: Studio Apartment Layout: Let the Furniture Draw the Rooms
pins.desc: A studio apartment layout works when the furniture does the dividing. Turn the sofa's back to the sleeping end, let a low shelf stand in for a wall, and lay a rug under the sitting area so the edge of the zone is visible from the door. Keep the walkway clear from the entry to the window and the room reads as three spaces instead of one crowded one. Contains affiliate links. #StudioApartment #SmallSpaceLiving #ApartmentLayout
pins.alt: A studio room seen from the doorway with a grey sofa backing onto a low shelf unit, a round jute rug and two knitted poufs marking the sitting area, a desk and chair under the window beyond, and a bed partly visible past a linen curtain.

pins.head: COUNT THE CUTS FIRST
pins.title: Cricut Vinyl Tips: Count the Cuts Before You Buy the Roll
pins.desc: Cricut vinyl tips that save money start with arithmetic. Lay your design out on paper, work out how many fit across the width of the roll, and you will know whether one roll covers the batch or you need two before the order goes in. Matte white permanent vinyl is the one most projects burn through first, so it is worth buying in a length you will actually finish. Contains affiliate links. #CricutProjects #VinylCrafts #CraftSupplies
pins.alt: A roll of matte white adhesive vinyl partly unrolled across a pale wood craft table with a second roll standing on its end behind it, a plain steel ruler lying across the unrolled sheet and a small wooden-handled weeding hook resting beside it.

pins.head: 6 CHECKS BEFORE YOU MIX
pins.title: Resin Bubbles: 6 Checks Before You Mix (Printable Checklist)
pins.desc: Resin bubbles are easier to prevent than to pop. Before you mix, run through 6 quick checks: product instructions open, measuring method confirmed, batch small enough for the working time, a compatible mixing cup, an approved bubble method and the room conditions noted. Tick them off on the page or print the list for your bench. Contains affiliate links. #ResinBubbles #EpoxyResin #ResinTips
pins.alt: A pin titled 6 Checks Before You Mix Resin over a photo of a clear cup of mixed resin with a wooden stir stick on a grey mat, with a card listing three checklist items with empty boxes and a note that three more checks are on the page.

pins.desc: Miniature painting tips start with the right supplies, and these 6 gifts cover the whole bench: a surface primer, a miniature brush set, a speedpaint starter set, a stay-wet palette, a brush washing container and a brush cleaner. Each one fixes a small frustration a painter already has. Contains affiliate links. #MiniaturePainting #GiftIdeas #TabletopGaming

pins.head: DECALS PER ROLL?
pins.title: Cricut Vinyl Tips: How Many 3-Inch Decals Fit on a 12-Inch Roll?
pins.desc: Cricut vinyl tips rarely include the math. Take a 12 inch by 5 foot roll, a 3 by 3 inch design and a quarter-inch gap: how many decals do you get? Type those numbers into the free calculator on the page and it counts them, tries the design turned 90 degrees and holds back spares for test cuts. Contains affiliate links. #CricutTips #VinylDecals #CricutProjects
